classification.difficultyReason: Find the shared pole height with tangent, then use that unrounded height in the second right triangle to determine the other ground distance.

content.prompt: From two points $A$ and $B$ on opposite sides of a telegraph pole, the angles of elevation of the top of the pole are found to be $40^\circ$ and $55^\circ$ respectively, as shown in the diagram below.

spec.description: Vertical pole between B on the left and A on the right; dashed sight lines, elevation arcs, point labels and a double-headed 25 m dimension below the pole-to-A segment.
spec.mathematics: A is 25 m from the foot. Elevations are 40 degrees at A and 55 degrees at B. Diagram coordinates derive from these angles.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied givens remain visible; no calculated lengths are shown.

children.prompt: If $A$ is $25\text{ m}$ from the base of the pole, find

children.label: a
children.prompt: the height of the pole to the nearest metre

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the height of the pole in metres.
$$\begin{align*}\tan40^\circ&=\frac{h}{25}\\h&=25\tan40^\circ\\h&\approx21\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: how far $B$ is from the base of the pole, to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the distance from $B$ to the base in metres. Use the unrounded height from part (a).
$$\begin{align*}\tan55^\circ&=\frac{25\tan40^\circ}{x}\\x&=\frac{25\tan40^\circ}{\tan55^\circ}\\x&\approx15\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre).}\end{align*}$$
